input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone today. I’ve tried a few times, but they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

I just checked my phone, and I noticed that there’s a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something important? Also, my Wi-Fi is off right now. I’m not sure about making calls or using the internet—should I try something?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said, and now I see some bars and something that says "5G" at the top. But I still can’t send picture messages—it's still not working. What should I do next?

I actually just checked that, and it says my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose my photos if we keep trying things?

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." I’m not sure if that’s right or not—does that look okay to you? What should I do next?

I don’t really know how to do that, and honestly, I get nervous about rebooting my phone. Will I lose any of my photos or messages if I reset the APN settings and restart the phone? Could you please reassure me and walk me through it step by step?

I followed your instructions and reset the APN settings, then restarted my phone. Unfortunately, I still can’t send picture messages—it’s still not working. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. Is there something else I should look at or try?

I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t seem to have storage or SMS permissions. Should I change something here? I’m not sure how to do that.

Alright, I’ve given my messaging app both the storage and SMS permissions like you said. Now it looks like I can send picture messages again! Thank you so much for your help and patience. Is there anything else I should do to make sure this keeps working?

Thank you so much for your help and for explaining everything so clearly. I really appreciate your patience with me—I get flustered with this stuff! I’ll keep your tips in mind if I have trouble again. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone today. I’ve tried a few times, but they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?

I can help you with that! To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either:

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin troubleshooting your MMS (picture messaging) issue.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you for providing your information, John. To help you fix the issue with sending picture messages (MMS), I’ll guide you through a few steps on your phone. 

First, could you please confirm:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send text messages?
- Are you able to use mobile data (for example, browse the internet when not on Wi-Fi)?

This will help me determine if the issue is specific to MMS or related to your general network or data connection.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Wi-Fi is turned OFF.

I just checked my phone, and I noticed that there’s a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something important? Also, my Wi-Fi is off right now. I’m not sure about making calls or using the internet—should I try something?

Yes, the airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless communications—including cellular service, mobile data, and MMS—are disabled. This is likely the reason you can’t send picture messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. After you do that, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still have trouble.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said, and now I see some bars and something that says "5G" at the top. But I still can’t send picture messages—it's still not working. What should I do next?

Thank you for turning off Airplane Mode and letting me know what you see. Next, I’d like to check if your phone is able to send MMS messages from a technical standpoint.

Could you please run a diagnostic check on your phone by using the “can_send_mms” function or tool (if available on your device)? This will help us determine if there are any technical issues preventing MMS from working.

If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know, and I can guide you through the next troubleshooting steps.

I actually just checked that, and it says my messaging app still can’t send MMS messages. Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose my photos if we keep trying things?

Thank you for checking that. Don’t worry—troubleshooting MMS issues will not delete or affect your photos stored on your phone.

The next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS problems. Could you please check your APN settings and let me know if you see any errors or if the MMSC URL is missing? If you’re unsure how to check, I can guide you through resetting your APN settings, which often resolves MMS issues.

Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." I’m not sure if that’s right or not—does that look okay to you? What should I do next?

Thank you for providing your APN details. The APN name and MMSC URL you shared look standard, but sometimes issues can still occur even if they appear correct.

The next recommended step is to reset your APN settings to the default values. This can resolve hidden configuration issues that might be affecting MMS. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your phone, or do you already know how to do this?

I don’t really know how to do that, and honestly, I get nervous about rebooting my phone. Will I lose any of my photos or messages if I reset the APN settings and restart the phone? Could you please reassure me and walk me through it step by step?

Rest assured, resetting your APN settings and rebooting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or personal data. These actions only affect your phone’s network connection settings and are safe to perform.

Here’s a step-by-step guide:

1. **Reset APN Settings:**
   - Go to your phone’s “Settings.”
   - Tap on “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
   - Select “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Networks.”
   - Tap on “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
   - Look for an option like “Reset to default” or “Reset settings” and select it.

2. **Reboot Your Phone:**
   - Hold down the power button on your phone until you see the option to restart or power off.
   - Select “Restart” or “Reboot.”

After your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if you need help with any of these steps or if you run into any issues.

APN settings will reset at reboot.

Restarting network services...

I followed your instructions and reset the APN settings, then restarted my phone. Unfortunately, I still can’t send picture messages—it’s still not working. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated.

Thank you for following the steps and letting me know the result. I understand this is frustrating, and I’m here to help you through it.

Let’s try a few more checks to pinpoint the issue:

1. Could you check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your phone? Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling turned on can interfere with sending MMS, especially if you’re not connected to Wi-Fi.
2. If Wi-Fi Calling is ON, please turn it OFF and try sending a picture message again.

Would you like instructions on how to check and turn off Wi-Fi Calling, or do you know how to do this?
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. Is there something else I should look at or try?

Thank you for confirming that Wi-Fi Calling is off. Next, let’s check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS, specifically access to storage and SMS.

Could you check your messaging app’s permissions and let me know if it has both “storage” and “SMS” permissions enabled? If you’re not sure how to check or change these permissions, I can guide you through the process. Would you like step-by-step instructions?

App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.

I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” It doesn’t seem to have storage or SMS permissions. Should I change something here? I’m not sure how to do that.

Yes, your messaging app needs both “storage” and “SMS” permissions to send and receive picture messages (MMS). Without these, MMS will not work.

Here’s how you can grant these permissions:

1. Go to your phone’s “Settings.”
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and select your messaging app (it might be called “Messages” or “Messaging”).
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Enable both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions by tapping on them and selecting “Allow.”

After granting these permissions, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need any help with these steps.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

Alright, I’ve given my messaging app both the storage and SMS permissions like you said. Now it looks like I can send picture messages again! Thank you so much for your help and patience. Is there anything else I should do to make sure this keeps working?

I'm glad to hear that granting the permissions fixed your picture messaging issue! There’s nothing else you need to do right now. As long as your messaging app keeps its storage and SMS permissions, and your phone’s network settings remain correct, MMS should continue to work.

If you ever have trouble again:
- Double-check that Airplane Mode is off.
- Make sure your messaging app still has the necessary permissions.
- Ensure your mobile data is enabled.

If you run into any more issues, feel free to reach out for help. Have a great day, and happy messaging!
